tool.name: RoadAnalysis
tool.summary:
Road network post-processing for semantic segmentation outputs (DeepLabV3 + PointRend, ResNet-101 backbone). Extracts road pixels from a single-band classified raster, applies morphological filtering (Majority Filter), vectorizes to polygons, simplifies boundaries (POINT_REMOVE) and dissolves adjacent segments into contiguous road features, computes geometry and Minimum Bounding Rectangle (MBR) attributes, enriches with nDSM height and thermal statistics, and classifies features as Road or Rejected possible road based on area, nDSM ceiling, MBR length, and MBR width thresholds. Optionally extracts polyline centerlines using a Voronoi medial axis algorithm (preferred) or morphological Thin (fallback). Produces a single output shapefile with accepted and rejected features, optional centerline polylines, optional centroid points, and a JSON run log.
Requires Spatial Analyst and 3D Analyst extensions.
PIPELINE (9 phases): Extract binary > Majority Filter > Vectorize > Simplify + Dissolve > Geometry and MBR > Enrichment (nDSM + Thermal) > Classification > Centerline Extraction (optional) > Export.
Roads differ from discrete objects (vehicles, buildings, trees) in that they are linear network features. Adjacent road polygons are dissolved into contiguous segments before classification. The nDSM threshold is inverted compared to buildings and trees: roads must be ground-level (nDSM below a ceiling), not elevated.
CENTERLINE METHODS: - Voronoi medial axis (primary): Densifies the polygon boundary, computes the Voronoi diagram (scipy), retains only interior edges, builds a networkx graph, and iteratively prunes short terminal branches. Handles junctions, bends, and variable widths natively. Requires shapely, scipy, networkx, numpy. - Morphological Thin (fallback): Rasterize > Thin > RasterToPolyline > Clip > TrimLine. Used when Voronoi dependencies are not available. Lower quality with possible spurs.
INPUTS: Classified Raster (single-band, integer), Road Class Value (from raster unique values), nDSM Raster (m), Thermal Raster (deg C, optional), Area of Interest (optional), Output CRS (optional).
OUTPUTS: road_results.shp (single layer with Class + Reason fields), road_centerlines.shp (polylines, optional), road_points.shp (centroids, optional), road_log.json.
FIELDS (polygons): RoadID, Area_m2, Perim_m, MBR_W, MBR_L, MBR_Azim, LW_Ratio, Compact, MEAN_nDSM, MEAN_Therm (if thermal provided), Class, Reason. FIELDS (centerlines): RoadID, Area_m2, Perim_m, MBR_W, MBR_L, MBR_Azim, LW_Ratio, Compact, MEAN_nDSM, MEAN_Therm, Class, Reason, CL_Len_m.
Part of the PostProcessing Toolbox (modular architecture: PostProcessing.pyt + _postproc_common.py + _road_core.py).
Developed by Nikolaos Koroniadis, MSc thesis, Geography and Applied Geoinformatics, University of the Aegean (https://geography.aegean.gr/geoinformatics/). Remote Sensing and GIS Research Group (https://rsgis.aegean.gr/).
tool.usage: Run from ArcGIS Pro Catalog: PostProcessing.pyt > Road > 4. Road Analysis. Select the classified raster, pick the road class value from the dropdown, provide an nDSM raster, and choose an output folder. The tool creates a roads subfolder with results. Optionally provide thermal data, an AOI mask, and a different output coordinate system. Enable Generate Centerline Polylines to extract the road network as polylines (Voronoi medial axis method). Review the road_log.json for full run parameters and statistics.

param.name: in_classified
param.dialogReference: Single-band classified raster with integer pixel values representing land cover classes. Each unique value is a different class. The tool extracts pixels matching the Road Class Value parameter. Must have at least 2 unique class values.

param.name: road_class
param.dialogReference: The pixel value in the classified raster that represents roads. When you select a classified raster, the unique class values found in the raster are listed as choices. Pick the value that corresponds to roads.

param.name: in_ndsm
param.dialogReference: Normalized Digital Surface Model, heights above ground in meters. Used for mean height per feature via Zonal Statistics. Roads are ground-level features: accepted road segments must have mean nDSM below the Maximum nDSM Height threshold. Typical road nDSM: 0.0-0.3 m.

param.name: in_thermal
param.dialogReference: Single-band thermal raster in degrees Celsius (Altum-PT LWIR). If provided, MEAN_Therm is computed per feature via Zonal Statistics. Asphalt roads typically show higher thermal signatures than surrounding vegetation.

param.name: in_aoi
param.dialogReference: Polygon or raster mask to clip the study area. If not set, the intersection of classified and nDSM extents is used.

param.name: out_crs
param.dialogReference: Coordinate reference system for all output shapefiles. Select from the globe icon or type an EPSG code (e.g. 2100 for EGSA87 / Greek Grid). Default: same as the classified raster. The CRS is applied only at the export phase to avoid raster reprojection issues during processing.

param.name: cell_size_option
param.dialogReference: Cell size for raster processing. Classified raster cell size (default, recommended) preserves full detail (~4.5 cm for Altum-PT). Maximum of inputs uses the coarsest resolution. Custom allows a user-defined value in meters.

param.name: cell_size_custom
param.dialogReference: User-defined cell size in meters. Only active when Processing Cell Size is set to Custom.

param.name: min_area
param.dialogReference: Road segments smaller than this area (m2) are classified as Rejected possible road with Reason = Area_below_min. Removes noise and small misclassified patches. After dissolve, road segments are typically much larger than this threshold. Default: 2.0.

param.name: max_ndsm
param.dialogReference: Maximum mean nDSM height for accepted roads. Features with mean nDSM above this value are classified as Rejected possible road with Reason = nDSM_above_max. Roads are ground-level: typical nDSM is 0.0-0.3 m. Elevated features (bridges, overpasses, misclassified buildings) are rejected. Default: 0.5.

param.name: reject_null_ndsm
param.dialogReference: If checked (default), features with no nDSM data (NULL) are classified as Rejected possible road with Reason = nDSM_null. If unchecked, they are kept as Road with Reason = nDSM_null_kept and a warning is logged. NULL nDSM occurs when a road segment falls outside the nDSM raster extent or on NoData pixels.

param.name: majority_neighborhood
param.dialogReference: Neighborhood for Majority Filter. FOUR (default): 4-connected, gentle. EIGHT: 8-connected, stronger but may erode narrow road segments. Skip: no filter applied.

param.name: majority_passes
param.dialogReference: Number of Majority Filter iterations. Each pass erodes edges by ~1 pixel. 1 (default) = light, 2 = moderate, 3+ = aggressive (may erode narrow roads). Disabled when Skip is selected. Warning: EIGHT with multiple passes may erode narrow road segments.

param.name: simplify_tol
param.dialogReference: Douglas-Peucker tolerance in meters for SimplifyPolygon (POINT_REMOVE). Smooths pixel-staircase boundaries before dissolve. 0.05 = minimal, 0.15 = moderate (default), 0.30 = cartographic. Applied before adjacent segments are dissolved together.

param.name: min_length
param.dialogReference: Minimum MBR length (longest side of Minimum Bounding Rectangle) for accepted roads. Features shorter than this are classified as Rejected possible road with Reason = Length_below_min. Removes small square patches that are unlikely to be real road segments. Default: 3.0.

param.name: min_width
param.dialogReference: Minimum MBR width (shortest side of Minimum Bounding Rectangle) for accepted roads. Features narrower than this are classified as Rejected possible road with Reason = Width_below_min. Typical single-lane road: 2.5-3.5 m, two-lane: 5.5-7.0 m. Default: 1.5.

param.name: do_centerlines
param.dialogReference: If checked (default), polyline centerlines are extracted from accepted road polygons. Primary method: Voronoi medial axis (requires shapely, scipy, networkx). Fallback: morphological Thin. Centerlines inherit parent polygon attributes via SpatialJoin and include CL_Len_m (length in meters). Output: road_centerlines.shp.

param.name: min_cl_length
param.dialogReference: Minimum length for centerline segments in meters. Centerlines shorter than this are removed. Filters out small stub centerlines from complex intersections. Default: 5.0. Located in the Centerline Parameters group.

param.name: max_hole_area
param.dialogReference: Interior holes in road polygons smaller than this area (m2) are filled before Voronoi centerline extraction. Vehicles, shadows, and small misclassified objects inside the road create holes that force the medial axis to branch around them. Filling small holes produces clean, straight centerlines. Default: 20.0 (covers most vehicles at ~12 m2).

param.name: prune_factor
param.dialogReference: Terminal branches in the Voronoi medial axis graph shorter than (prune_factor x median MBR width) are iteratively removed. Controls how aggressively short spurs are pruned. Lower values keep more detail; higher values produce cleaner centerlines. Default: 2.0.

param.name: densify_factor
param.dialogReference: The polygon boundary is sampled at intervals of (densify_factor x cell size) meters before computing the Voronoi diagram. Lower values produce a finer medial axis (more computation); higher values are faster but less precise. The interval is clamped to a minimum of 0.15 m. Default: 5.0.

param.name: do_centroids
param.dialogReference: Creates road_points.shp with one centroid per road polygon (all features: accepted and rejected). Attributes carried over. Useful for heatmaps, density analysis, web maps.

param.name: out_folder
param.dialogReference: Root folder for results. A roads subfolder is created. Outputs: road_results.shp, road_centerlines.shp (optional), road_points.shp (optional), road_log.json. Existing outputs are overwritten.
